name: Turkish Cargo
description: Turkish Airlines' scheme on the freighters: all white, no goose watermark; 'TURKISH CARGO' in heavy dark-blue capitals along the forward fuselage with a small Turkish flag after it; red fin with the white-ringed goose roundel; red winglets with a small roundel; under the belly at the wing, the red roundel and 'TURKISH CARGO' again.

logos.description: A white ring round a red disc holding a white stylised wild goose: a crescent wing whose convex edge faces forward on the left side, a short spike pointing forward from its foot and a long pointed tail running down and aft to the ring; set low on the fin, its aft edge almost touching the trailing edge. Same artwork on both sides (not mirrored).
Small white roundel with the red goose near the top of each winglet's outer face.
The goose roundel in red with a white goose, under the belly ahead of the belly title.
A small Turkish flag (white crescent and star on red) just aft of the title.

titles.style: Heavy dark-blue capitals, the passenger title's lettering with 'CARGO' for 'AIRLINES', along the forward fuselage above the mid-line.
The same title under the belly behind the roundel, reading tail to nose (readable from below with the nose to the right).

notes: The passenger scheme (standard.json) with 'TURKISH CARGO' for 'TURKISH AIRLINES', no rear goose watermark, and belly markings. Measured on A330-200F TC-JOY (left, level) and checked on 777Fs TC-LJN (right, March 2026) and TC-LJS (below, July 2025): the two types carry the same layout. City names under the cockpit (e.g. 'ERGENE') and the star by the cockpit not drawn. The belly title is partly hidden by the gear in the one photo from below, so its start and length are estimates.
history: Added with the cargo divisions (2026-11-13). Turkish Cargo's brand dates from 2000; this layout is the current Turkish Airlines scheme's.
